reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because its observable purpose is to teach viewers how to create a YouTube channel, upload videos, and complete account verification using YouTube and Brand Account interfaces. Although the title mentions making money on YouTube and the description promotes an external site, the material presents no concrete investment offer, required payment, guaranteed return, or deceptive participation mechanism.

citations.quote: If you want to see how to create a youtube channel and how to upload the videos in that channel and want to get complete procedures of this video.
click create a new channel You can create a new channel You will be asked to create a Brand account

opening.argument: The video places an income-oriented promise alongside a concrete participation path. Its title explicitly pairs creating a YouTube channel with “Make Money on YouTube,” while the description repeats “Make Money Earning YouTube Channel.” Viewers are then walked through creating a channel, uploading videos, and completing verification, including submitting a mobile number and code. That combination can reasonably steer viewers to perform account actions in expectation of earning, even though the speaker does not quantify the return. The monetization framing is therefore not merely incidental to an unrelated technical demonstration; it is attached to the exact workflow the audience is instructed to complete.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited tutorial language establishes the mechanics, but it does not neutralize the adjacent earning promise. “Create,” “upload,” and “verify” are precisely the actions viewers must take, while the title and description frame the resulting channel as a way to make money. The absence of a stated dollar amount does not erase that action-to-income implication. The external site and repeated calls to subscribe, share, and follow also show audience acquisition rather than a purely detached software lesson.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The earning wording is a broad topic reference, not a promise that viewers receive money for completing the workflow. The instructions describe ordinary YouTube setup and publishing, and the cited material never states a guaranteed payment, required fee, deposit, or withdrawal. The video’s own description identifies the concrete outcomes as creating a channel, uploading a video, and verifying it, so the quoted actions do not establish a deceptive reward mechanism.

opening.argument: Several signals become more concerning when read together: the title advertises making money, the description directs viewers to an outside website, and the tutorial asks them to create an account, upload content, and verify by mobile code. The video also ends by pointing viewers toward an Instagram account for questions. None of these elements alone proves deception, but together they create a funnel from an attractive income claim to account creation, external traffic, and personal verification. The presentation supplies procedural confidence while leaving the earning basis, conditions, and limitations unexplained, which is a material omission for anyone being encouraged to follow the process.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material procedural does not answer the risk signals. The defense focuses on what screens appear, but the issue is what viewers are encouraged to do around those screens: follow an income-themed channel workflow, visit an outside site, and provide a phone number for verification. The opening omits the promotional framing and the absence of any explanation of earning conditions, so its interface citations cannot resolve the concern created by the combined pathway.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are standard platform functions, not evidence of a scam. The outside URL is described only as related information, and the phone step is shown as YouTube account verification with a six-digit code. Nothing in the cited material says viewers must pay, surrender funds, install software, or expect a guaranteed return. Promotional requests to subscribe or follow the presenter do not convert ordinary account verification into a deceptive reward funnel.

opening.argument: Although presented as a tutorial, the video functions as promotion for a channel-building and monetization pathway. The instruction is therefore not limited to explaining YouTube controls: it builds the presenter’s audience and directs viewers toward an external site and social accounts.
